entries.title: Practice the beliefs
entries.summary: Read the statement of belief slowly and carry one belief into the rest of the day.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Choose a single line from Jedi Believe to remember when your attention gets scattered.

entries.title: Return to Focus, Knowledge, and Wisdom
entries.summary: Revisit the Three Tenets and notice which one best fits today’s responsibilities.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Name the tenet you most need today before you open the full source reading.

entries.title: Sit with the Jedi Code
entries.summary: Read both public formulations of the Code and pay attention to the line that feels most active today.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Compare the two formulations and keep one line as a practical anchor for the day.

entries.title: Meditate with the prayer
entries.summary: Use the public meditation text as a slow reading practice before moving into the rest of your routine.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Read one stanza out loud or in silence, then continue to the full source text if you want the whole prayer.

entries.title: Read one teaching with care
entries.summary: Open the teachings and spend time with just one numbered teaching instead of racing through the list.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Pick one teaching to revisit at the end of the day and notice whether it changed your choices.

entries.title: Study one maxim in context
entries.summary: Choose a maxim, read its note, and let that pairing shape the day’s practice.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Notice whether the maxim’s note deepens or complicates the surface reading.

entries.title: Hold the Knight’s Code lightly
entries.summary: Use the Knight’s Code as bonus study for companion reflection alongside doctrine reading.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Read it as companion material and hold it as supplemental reading while you reflect.

entries.title: Practice courage with a selected sermon
entries.summary: Use this sermon reference to reflect on fear, courage, and one action you can take with more honesty today.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Name one place where fear has slowed you down, then carry one concrete act of courage into the day.
